post.summary: Enters today's spot rates in one go (1 unit of each currency = the rate in the company's currency) into the organization's rates, a reason being needed to correct one already entered today, and returns the day's rates

AccountFilter.description: Which accounts a row adds up: by type, subtype, category, posting role, a code range or named codes; exclusions narrow any of them. Empty means every account.

AdjustPriceListRequest.description: Every price in a list changed by a percentage (a yearly increase), rounded to an increment when one is given.

AdvancePurchaseShipmentRequest.description: Moves the shipment forward to in_production, shipped, at_port or customs on a date, with a note (container, vessel, broker).

AgingRow.description: One supplier's payables at a date, in the company's currency, by days past due; advances are shown apart because they sit on their own control account.

AllocatableReceiptLine.description: A posted receipt line a landed cost can be allocated to, with the basis values it would count with.

AllocatedNumber.description: An allocated number: the series that issued it, its sequence within the reset period, and the rendered text.

ApplyReceivableRequest.description: Applies a credit note, a receipt on account or a deposit to an invoice open item of the same customer and currency; a rate difference is realised FX, booked by the subledger itself.

ApplyRequest.description: Applies a debit note, a payment on account or an advance to an invoice open item of the same supplier and currency.

ApproverSpecRequest.description: Who approves: named members, or every active holder of a role (scoped to the document's company unless told otherwise).

ArAgingRow.description: One customer's receivables at a date, in the company's currency, by days past due; deposits are shown apart because they sit on their own control account.

ArStatementCurrency.description: The account in one of the documents' currencies: what was owed before the period, the period's movements and what is owed at its end.

ArStatementLine.description: One movement on a customer's account: a document booked (what they owe goes up for an invoice, down for a credit note or a receipt) or its reversal.

AssetBookValueRequest.description: How one book values the asset, where it departs from the category's defaults; blanks take the defaults.

AutoMatchResult.description: What the matcher did on a statement or an account: lines paired, movements created, lines left for a person.

BomRequirement.description: A component requirement for a quantity of output, in the component's base unit, exact before scrap and after it.

BounceChequeRequest.description: A received cheque the bank returned unpaid: what the bank charged, and what is re-charged to the customer as a new receivable.

CalculatedField.description: A field computed after aggregation from the measures of the row: arithmetic over their keys, such as `(net_amount - cost_amount) / net_amount * 100`.

ChangeOrderRequest.description: A change order: the same shape as a save, plus why; the previous revision is kept and the order goes through approval again.

ChartOptions.description: How a saved report draws: the chart type, whether series stack, which dimension gives the categories and which the series, and which measures plot.

ChequeActionRequest.description: A step of a cheque's life on a date: clearing or paying (with what the bank charged), or cancelling an issued one.

ChequeDetailsRequest.description: The cheque behind a receipt or payment by cheque: its number (or the book an issued one takes it from), the drawer and the due date (post-dated when after the document's date).

ChequeForecastRow.description: Cheques falling due in a month: what is expected in from customers and out to suppliers, in the company's currency.

CodeSuggestion.description:
For a code being typed on a new or edited record: whether it is already taken in its scope (case-insensitively, the
record itself excepted), and the next free code, continuing the most common pattern of the existing codes
(CUS-0041 after CUS-0040, WH30 after WH10 and WH20) or, for an account, its siblings under the parent.

ColumnParameters.description: What a column needs besides its type: the two columns a variance compares (`Of` minus `Against`), or the fixed dates of a custom range.

CommissionBand.description: One band of a commission: the part of the basis that fell between two thresholds, at its rate.

CommissionEntrySummary.description: What a sales rep earned on a line of the invoice under their plan, in the plan's currency.

CommissionQuote.description:
What a sale earns under a plan: the scope that matched (the most specific rules for the item's category and the
customer's group), the bands the sale crossed given the rep's basis so far in the tier period, and the total rounded
in the plan's currency. A negative basis (a credit note) gives back what the same bands earned.

ComplianceCheck.description: One sample document the compliance checks sent and what the scheme answered.

CopyPrintTemplateRequest.description: A copy of a template for a company or a branch, starting from the source's current version.

CorrectEntryRequest.description: The replacement of an entry (its lines as a posting request; the company is the original's) and why.

CreateFromLineRequest.description: A movement the books lacked, made from a statement line: a bank charge, interest, or another income or expense by its account role.

CreditStatusRequest.description: status on_hold (new orders wait for release) or blocked (orders, shipments and invoices refused), with a reason; ok releases.

Customer360.description:
The partner at a glance: its record with contacts, addresses and the accounts the member may read; its pipeline;
open and recent activities; and each module's balances and latest documents with it.

Customer360Pipeline.description: Open opportunities with their totals per currency, those closed in the last year, and the win rate over them.

CustomFieldHostList.description: The record types that carry custom fields, in code order.

CustomFieldRules.description: Type-specific rules: number range, text length and pattern, the entity type a reference points at.

DiscardOutboxMessageRequest.description: Why an operator gives up on a dead letter; kept on the message.

DocumentFlow.description:
The purchasing documents connected to one document: where it came from (requisition, request for quotation,
blanket agreement, order) and what followed (receipts, returns, landed costs, invoices and debit notes), limited to
what the member may read. bool DocumentFlow.Truncated says the chain was cut at int DocumentFlowService.MaxOrders orders.

DocumentSearchHit.description: A numbered document found by its number: its type and id (to open it), the number, its company and when it was issued.

DraftIdentifier.description: The identifier a draft shows until numbering issues its number.

DrillRequest.description: The lines behind a cell: the query's filters plus the cell's dimension keys (a null key means the rows where that dimension is empty).

DunningLetterItem.description: One overdue item as a letter names it: what was open on the date, how late, and the level it reached.

DunningPreview.description: What a run on the date would issue, before anything is written.

DunningRunRequest.description: Issues the letters due on a date for the company's overdue customers, or one customer; fees are charged unless told otherwise.

EinvoicePreview.description: The XML of a document as the scheme would receive it, before any submission: to inspect what the adapter builds.

EmployeeComponentRequest.description: A component the employee carries, with the amount or rate that overrides the component's default when given.

ExpenseSummary.description:
An expense as the screens read it. PaymentStatus is derived from the payable: `unpaid`,
`partial`, `paid`, or `n/a` for a petty cash voucher (paid when it was incurred) and for anything not
yet confirmed.

FefoSuggestion.description: One lot a first-expiry-first-out plan would take from, and how much (roadmap 3.5).

FinishCountRequest.description: Finishing a count in one step (trader edition, ADR-0035 §9): the reason every difference takes when its line has none (the shipped COUNT reason by default), a note for it, and whether the lines nobody counted are taken as unchanged.

FlowDocument.description: One document of a purchasing flow, as the smart buttons and the flow list show it.

FundSummary.description: A fund with where it stands: its balance from the cash box's movements, and how far below the float it is.

Grant.description: A permission grant with the scopes it applies to (union of all assignments that grant it).

HealthReportView.description: The health payload: a status word, the applied migrations (when the database answers), an error name and each check.

HomeCash.description: The balance of every active bank account and cash box at the date, and what came in and went out this month.

HomeDashboard.description:
The home page's numbers for one company on one day (founder programme item 1): what was sold, what is owed and
due, the money in the bank and the cash boxes, and the documents waiting for the next step. A section is null when
the member may not read what it counts. Amounts are in the company's functional currency and come straight from
the modules' tables (posted invoices, open items, bank transactions), so they agree with the screens they open.

HomePayables.description: What is owed to suppliers as the open items stand now: past due at the date, due within the seven days after it, and in all.

HomePipeline.description: Documents waiting for their next step; a count is null when the member may not read that document type.

HomeReceivables.description: What customers owe as the open items stand now: past due at the date, due within the seven days after it, and in all.

HomeSales.description: Net sales (invoices less credit notes, before tax) of the day, the month so far and the same days of the month before, with a day-by-day series for the last thirty days.

InboundCostAdjustmentRequest.description: A late supplier invoice (`invoice`: the actual unit cost replaces the expected one) or a landed cost (`landed_cost`: an amount added to the layer).

InspectSalesReturnRequest.description: The inspection's verdict per line; the date is the posting date of what it moves (scrap) and defaults to today.

InvariantReport.description: A run of the harness for one tenant (optionally one company): every check with its outcome.

InvariantResult.description: One check: what it looked at, whether it holds, and the first problems it found (never more than a page).

InvoicableLine.description: What can still be invoiced for a supplier: posted receipt lines with an uninvoiced quantity and open service lines of orders.

InvoicableSalesLine.description: What can still be invoiced to a customer: posted shipment lines with an uninvoiced quantity and open service lines of its orders; quantities in the item's base unit.

ItemCostInfo.description: The cost of an item in one cost scope at a date: the running quantity, value and average, the last and the standard cost.

ItemImportResult.description: What an import did, or would do when bool ItemImportResult.DryRun: nothing was kept, the counts say what a real run would create and update.

JobRecord.description: A stored job as the runner and the UI see it.

LayoutOptions.description: The choices a designer offers: the chart's account types, subtypes, categories and posting roles.

LayoutRowDefinition.description: A row of a layout: a header, an account selection, a formula over other rows' codes, or a blank line.

LayoutSummary.description: A layout as listed: a shipped one has no id and `IsSystem`; a tenant's has an id and may be unpublished.

LedgerDrill.description:
What a figure drills to: the ledger of the account over the same window with the same dimension filters and, for
a row of a built-in grouping, that grouping's value (query keys `g.KEY=value`; `~` for lines without one).

LineBestOffer.description: The cheapest landed unit price offered for one request line, among the offers whose minimum the line reaches.

LoginResponse.description: Login outcome: a token set, a tenant choice, an MFA challenge or an MFA enrollment requirement.

LotTrace.description: Where a lot came from, where it went, where it is, and who received it (hard scenario 12).

MentionableMember.description: A member a comment can mention: the name only, so commenting does not reveal the workspace's email addresses.

MoveOpportunityRequest.description: Moves the opportunity to a stage; a lost stage needs the reason; the probability defaults to the stage's.

NettingRequest.description: Sets a customer's open receivable item against the same partner's open payable item, in their common currency; the amount defaults to the smaller remainder.

NotificationOutcome.description: How many in-app rows were written and how many emails were queued after preferences.

NumberPreview.description: The series a request would use and the text its next number would have (no lock, no allocation).

OpenFiscalYearRequest.description: Opens the fiscal year that starts in StartYear (on the calendar's start month) as `open` or `future`.

OpeningBalanceResult.description:
What an opening-balance import did, or would do when bool OpeningBalanceResult.DryRun: the journal posted (none on a dry run),
both sides, the difference opening balance equity absorbed, and how many lines and partners were involved.

OpeningBalanceRow.description: One line of an opening-balance import: the account by code, one side, and what its control needs: the partner's code with the due date, or the bank account or cash box's code.

OpenOrderLine.description: One order line with goods still to arrive: what was ordered, what came, what is open and whether it is late.

OrderSuggestionsRequest.description: Replenishment suggestions to order; suggestions without a supplier take SupplierId.

discardedAt.description: When an operator discarded the dead letter; its aggregate's later events no longer wait for it.

OutboxMessage.description: A stored outbox row as the dispatcher and the operator UI see it.

PageOfActivityView.description: One page of a list: the items and the opaque cursor of the next page (null on the last page).

PageOfCostAdjustmentRunInfo.description: One page of a list: the items and the opaque cursor of the next page (null on the last page).

PageOfDeliverySummary.description: One page of a list: the items and the opaque cursor of the next page (null on the last page).

PageOfItemSummary.description: One page of a list: the items and the opaque cursor of the next page (null on the last page).

PageOfJournalEntrySummary.description: One page of a list: the items and the opaque cursor of the next page (null on the last page).

PageOfManualJournalSummary.description: One page of a list: the items and the opaque cursor of the next page (null on the last page).

PageOfNotificationView.description: One page of a list: the items and the opaque cursor of the next page (null on the last page).

PageOfPartnerSummary.description: One page of a list: the items and the opaque cursor of the next page (null on the last page).

PageOfStockLedgerRow.description: One page of a list: the items and the opaque cursor of the next page (null on the last page).

PageOfStockSearchRow.description: One page of a list: the items and the opaque cursor of the next page (null on the last page).

PartnerBalance.description: What is open with a partner in one company and currency: the amount in that currency and in the company's, what is past due, how many items, the oldest due date.

PartnerDocument.description: One of the partner's documents as the module that owns it shows it in the 360 view.

PartnerImportResult.description: What an import did, or would do when bool PartnerImportResult.DryRun: partners created and updated, company accounts kept, rows in all.

PartnerImportRow.description: One partner of an import: the partner itself and, for the company the import names, its account's currency, terms, limit and groups by code.

PayExpenseRequest.description: A payment of a confirmed supplier or employee expense from a bank account on a day; the whole remainder unless an amount is given.

PaymentInstalment.description: One instalment of a payment schedule: its share and the amount after the currency's rounding (the parts sum to the whole).

PayPurchaseShipmentCostRequest.description: Pays one cost of the journey to its agent from a cash box or bank account in the company's currency; the agent is named here when the cost does not name one yet.

PayPurchaseShipmentRequest.description:
Pays the supplier for the goods from a cash box or bank account (ADR-0035 §11): the amount in the order's currency
(the rest of the goods when none is given); when the account is in the company's currency and the order is not,
what left the account in that currency (the rate actually paid). Before the supplier's invoice it is an advance,
applied to the invoice when that is posted; after, a payment of the invoice.

PeriodGaps.description: Gapless audit for one reset period of a series: what was issued and which numbers are missing (expected: none).

PermissionDefinition.description: A permission the system understands: a stable key, its module and a human description.

PickLineRequest.description:
What a picker confirms for one line: the quantity taken, and where from when it differs from the plan
            (another bin, another lot); a serial-tracked item names the serials scanned. Less than planned is a short pick and
            says why; zero is "nothing there".

PickListRow.description: A pick list in a work queue: its progress without its lines.

PipelineBoard.description: The board: every active stage in order with its opportunities (won and lost columns show the last 90 days) and the open pipeline's totals.

PipelineTotal.description: A total of opportunities in one currency: how many, their expected amount and the probability-weighted amount.

PosCatalogue.description: What a till needs to sell offline: the register's rules and every sellable item priced and taxed as of now.

PosCatalogueItem.description: One sellable entry of the catalogue a till caches: an item, or one variant of it, in its sales unit, with the price and the tax the till applies offline.

PostingWindowRequest.description: One allow-posting window: for everyone when RoleId is null, else for that role; at least one bound.

PriceCandidate.description: A rule or source the engine looked at for a step and what became of it.

PriceFact.description: A fact behind a step (a rate, a quantity break, a rounding), as an invariant string for display.

PriceFloorCheck.description: The line's price against the floor that governs it (the item's, else its nearest category's).

PriceProblem.description: Why a line could not be priced; the steps before the problem stay in the explanation.

PriceStep.description:
One step of a line's price (ADR-0030): what it started from and ended at (unit price for the price steps, the line's
running net for the discount steps), the amount it took off, the rule or source that decided it, the facts behind it
and the other candidates considered.

PricingLineRequest.description: One line to price: an item (or one of its variants) in one of its units; no unit means the item's sales unit, else its base unit.

PricingRequest.description:
A basket to price for a customer (or no one in particular) in a company on a date. The currency defaults to the
customer's account currency, else the company's; the pricing date to today in the company; the tax basis to the
basis of the prices found.

PricingResult.description: A priced basket: every line with its explanation, the promotions and document discounts applied, and the totals.

PrintRequest.description: What to print: the document, the variant (tax invoice or pro forma), and which template when not the default.

PrintShareRequest.description: A link to a ready render for someone without an account: the channel it goes by (link or whatsapp), the phone it is for, and how long it lives (1 to 30 days).

PrintShareSummary.description: A share link; the URL is given once, on creation, since only the token's hash is kept.

ProjectionRun.description: What a refresh did: rows added or updated per fact.

ProjectionStatus.description: The state of one fact's projection for the tenant.

PromiseToPayRequest.description: A promise to pay on an item: the date the customer promised, and what they said; a null date clears the promise.

PurchaseAnalysisRow.description: One group of a purchase analysis: a supplier, an item or a month, with its orders and values in the company's currency.

PurchaseShipmentCostSummary.description: A cost of the journey: who it is paid to, the agent's invoice once the goods arrived, and the payment that paid it (none while unpaid).

PurchaseShipmentHint.description: Something the trader should look at, as a code the client words: arrival_overdue (days), no_costs, payment_missing, rate_above_order (percent), rate_below_order (percent), invoice_missing, stale (days).

PurchaseShipmentLineSummary.description: One ordered item with its share of the goods paid and of the costs, in the company's currency, and the landed cost of one unit.

PurchaseShipmentPaymentSummary.description: One payment made from the shipment, as Banking posted it.

PurchaseShipmentSummary.description: A shipment as its screen shows it. `GoodsOutstandingTc` is what the posted supplier invoice still asks for (whoever paid the rest), before the invoice the order's total less the shipment's own payments; `GoodsPaidTc` is the goods total less that.

QueryDefinition.description:
A query over a semantic model (ADR-0034 §3): the dimensions on rows and columns, the measures, the filters, the
sort and top-N, calculated fields, an optional comparison (prior_period or prior_year), and the date range on
the model's date (the year to date when none is given). The company is always named; the reader's scopes apply.

QueryExplanation.description: The compiled statement with its parameters, and the same statement with the values written in for reading.

QueryFilter.description: A filter on a dimension: operators eq, ne, in, not_in, gt, gte, lt, lte, between, contains, starts_with, is_null, not_null; values typed by the field.

QueryValue.description: A measure to aggregate; the aggregation defaults to the field's own.

QuickExpenseRequest.description:
An expense in one step, as a shop records it (ADR-0035 §12, A-195): what for (the category), how much in the company's
currency, when, paid from which bank account or cash box (or not yet), and to whom. A payee is needed unless the
money left a cash box.

QuickPurchaseCostRequest.description: A cost of bringing the goods in (freight, duty, port, transport) in its currency, owed to its agent when one is named.

QuickPurchaseLineRequest.description: One item bought: the quantity in the item's unit (or the one named) at the supplier's unit price in the purchase currency.

QuickPurchaseRequest.description:
Goods bought and already in hand, recorded in one step (trader edition, ADR-0035 §22): the supplier, the store, the
day, the items at their prices in the purchase currency, the journey's costs, the supplier's invoice number.

QuickSaleRequest.description: A sale done in one step (trader edition, ADR-0035 §6): the goods leave the warehouse and the invoice is posted at once.

QuoteRanking.description:
One quote in the comparison: the landed total in the company's currency, the rate used, the rank and why.
MeetsMoq is false when a line is offered only from a minimum the request does not reach
(MoqShortfallLines names them); PremiumPct is how much dearer than the first-ranked
quote this one lands, in percent, for the quotes that price every line.

QuoteRecommendation.description:
The quote to order from and why, in reason codes the client words: cheapest_landed, complete, meets_moq, fastest,
only_offer. SavingVsNextRc is what it saves against the next complete, feasible quote;
SplitSavingRc what buying each line from its cheapest feasible offer would save against ordering
everything from the recommended one (null when nothing).

ReceivableLine.description: An open order line as the receiving screen sees it: what was ordered, what arrived so far and what the tolerance still allows.

RecordRef.description: A record another module owns, as a pricing screen shows it.

RecordScopes.description: Record scopes attached to a principal's grants; an empty set for a scope type means "all".

RecurringInvoiceRun.description: One recurring invoice's run: generated (the invoice), or waiting with the problem that stopped it.

RecurringLineRequest.description: A template line: amounts in fixed mode, percentages of the base amount in percentage mode (debit or credit side), accounts only in variable mode.

ReorderStagesRequest.description: The stages in the order the board shows them; every stage of the tenant, each once.

ResultField.description: A column of a result: a dimension (its label column; the key travels as `<key>_key`), a measure, a calculated field, or a comparison column (`group` prior or change).

ReturnableLine.description: A posted receipt line with something left to return, and what has already gone back.

ReturnableSalesLine.description: A posted shipment line of a customer with goods not yet returned: what can still come back, and which serials.

RoleTemplateInfo.description:
A starting point for a role: the grants a typical job needs, copied into a new role and edited there. Grants name
permissions that exist today; pending grants name areas of modules not yet available, which the system role of the
same template already holds and a new role can be given once the module ships.

RoutineOutcome.description: One item the routine handled: what it targeted, what it produced, or why it waited.

RoutineRunItem.description:
One item of a logged run: `kind` reversal (target: the entry reversed), recurring (the template; produces a
journal) or deferral (the schedule; produces an entry), the target's number or code when it has one, and the outcome.

RoutineRunResult.description: What one run of the daily routines did for a company (or a tenant when Guid? RoutineRunResult.CompanyId is null).

RoutineRunSummary.description: A logged run of the daily routines for one company.

RuleConditions.description: What a rule looks for in a line: words in its text, a pattern on its reference, a side and an amount range.

RunDashboardRequest.description: Runs a dashboard for a company over a period: the dashboard's default period, another named one, or fixed dates (`custom`).

RunReportRequest.description: Overrides when running a saved report: another company, another range; everything else is the saved definition.

SalesLineRow.description:
One line of a sales invoice or credit note with everything it can be grouped or filtered by (founder programme
item 1f: group by customer, item, rep, month and some thirty more): the document, its customer and their set-up,
the item and its catalogue, the tax, the dimensions, and the amounts. A credit note's quantities and amounts are
negative, so sums net out. Names are in both languages as the records hold them.

SalesLinesReport.description: The lines asked for, in posting order; bool SalesLinesReport.Truncated says the cap was hit and a narrower range is needed.

SalesReturnAppliedEntry.description:
A shipment ledger entry the return applies to: the entry, its serial and how much of it came back; once
            received, the return's own inbound entry that brought it back and where it was put (what scrap and reversal apply to).

SaveBankAccountRequest.description: Numbers are sent in clear over TLS once and stored only encrypted; omit them on an update to keep what is stored.

SaveCarrierRequest.description: The carrier and its tracking reference, often only known once the goods have left.

SaveCommissionRuleRequest.description: One band: for sales in the item category (and its descendants) and/or the customer group, from a period-to-date amount upwards.

SaveCustomerAccountRequest.description:
The partner as a customer of one company. Blank terms and posting default from the group. The credit fields
(limit in the company's functional currency, empty for none; exposure basis; overdue days that block) change only
with `partners.credit.manage`; send them as they stand otherwise.

SaveCustomerReceiptRequest.description:
A customer receipt: lines settle invoice open items (amount, early-payment discount given, tax the customer withheld),
the remainder goes on account; a deposit (kind `customer_deposit`) has no lines. Charges are what the bank kept,
in the bank account's currency; the bank amount is what it credited and is required when that currency differs
from the receipt's.

SaveExpenseLineRequest.description: One line of an expense: the category decides the account (and the usual tax code unless the line names one); dimensions by code.

SaveExpenseRequest.description:
An expense to record: owed to a supplier or an employee (PartnerId), or paid from a petty cash
fund (FundId); dated the day it was incurred, in the currency it was incurred in.

SaveInvoiceLineRequest.description: A line: against a posted receipt line (three-way), an order line without a receipt (services, two-way) or a free expense line on an account role; quantity and price in the invoice currency.

SaveItemUomRequest.description: 1 Uom = Numerator / Denominator base units (24 pieces per carton: 24/1; 1 piece = 1/24 carton is never stored, the inverse is derived).

SavePackagesRequest.description: The shipment's packages as a whole: what is sent replaces what was there.

SavePaymentRequest.description:
A supplier payment: lines settle invoice open items (amount, early-payment discount, withholding at payment), the
remainder goes on account; an advance (kind `supplier_advance`) has no lines. Charges and the bank amount are
in the bank account's currency; the bank amount is required when that differs from the payment currency.

SavePrintTemplateRequest.description: An edit of a template: a new version of its HTML and CSS, and the settings that are not versioned.

SavePurchaseShipmentCostRequest.description: A cost of the journey: its charge type, amount and currency; the rate actually paid, or the spot rate of the day when none is given.

SaveRegisterRequest.description: A register to create or change; the code is given or taken from the name; decimal? SaveRegisterRequest.CashRoundingIncrement null or 0 means the company's setting for the currency.

SaveSalesReturnLineRequest.description:
One shipment line's goods coming back on a sales return (roadmap 5.8a). The quantity is in the item's base unit like
the shipment line's own; a serial-tracked line names the serials coming back; a reason code of the inventory
catalogue (`return`) and free text say why; the disposition proposed here is settled at inspection; the bin is
where the goods are put away (the shipment's own bin when none is named); the unit cost, in the company's currency,
counts only under the `specified` cost policy.

SaveShipmentLineRequest.description:
A shipment line's quantity is always the item's base unit, exactly like the reservation and
            `qty_shipped` it consumes (A-152's own reasoning extended here) -- there is no unit to convert.

ScheduleRecipient.description: Who a schedule sends to: a member (by membership, at the address on their profile at run time) or an outside address.

ScheduleRunRequested.description: What a "run now" returns: the job that will run the schedule.

SellerDetails.description: The seller as the scheme prints it on every invoice of the device: the commercial registration and the address parts ZATCA requires.

SerialHistory.description: The serial and everything that happened to it, oldest first (hard scenario 13: one screen, one query).

SetCounterRequest.description: Moves a counter; moving it backwards needs the reset permission and a reason and never below a number already issued.

SetPurchaseShipmentPaymentRequest.description: What was paid for the goods in the company's currency (null clears it); the effective rate follows from it.

SetupStatus.description:
Where a tenant stands on the way to its first posted document (setup wizard, A-173): what exists already, counted
so a step can show itself done. Company-bound parts (the chart, the opening journal) read for the company asked
for, or the tenant's first company when none is.

ShipmentAllocation.description:
One part of a shipment line's quantity: the bin and lot it comes from, its serials, and once posted the
            stock ledger entries it produced (what a reversal returns, entry by entry).

SignupRequest.description: A new workspace with its owner; Edition is the shell it opens in from the start (`full`, or `trader` in the trader program's own stack, ADR-0035 §19).

SlowMovingReport.description: Stock idle for at least int SlowMovingReport.MinIdleDays days at DateOnly SlowMovingReport.AsOf, the longest idle first; the value total only when costs may be seen.

SlowMovingRow.description:
One item's stock in one warehouse that has not been used for a while: what is on hand at the date, when it first and
last came in, when it was last sold or consumed, how many days it has been idle (since the last use, or since it
first came in when it never was) and, for those who may see costs, its value.

SodExceptionSummary.description: An exception to a segregation-of-duties rule for one member: why, who allowed it, until when, and whether it was revoked.

StatementCurrency.description: The account in one of the documents' currencies: what was owed before the period, the period's movements and what is owed at its end.

StatementDesignPreview.description: A designer's preview: the statement computed from a definition that is not saved yet.

StatementDrill.description: The accounts behind one cell with the column's window, so each can open in the ledger over the same dates.

StatementLine.description: One movement on a supplier's account: a document booked (what we owe goes up for an invoice, down for a debit note or a payment) or its reversal.

StatementMappingSettings.description: How a bank's CSV export reads: columns by header name or 1-based position, and how dates and numbers are written.

StatementPreviewRequest.description: A CSV read with a mapping before it is imported: the first lines as they would be taken, or why they cannot be.

StatementRequest.description:
Running a statement: the company, the layout (a tenant's by id or a shipped one by code), the period (its end
defaults to today in the company's time zone, its start to the fiscal period that holds the end), dimension
filters applied to every row, and whether closing entries count (a balance sheet includes them by default, the
profit and loss and the trial balance leave them out, as the ledger inquiry does).

StockSearchRow.description: One row per item and warehouse for the global stock search: what is there, what is promised, what can be taken.

StockValueEntryInfo.description: One value entry of a stock ledger entry, with the reason it exists.

SubmitOrderLineRequest.description: A line as the till sold it: the unit price it charged (the catalogue's unless the cashier overrode it), the discount, and the tax code the catalogue gave the item.

SubmitOrderRequest.description:
An order as the till synced it. string SubmitOrderRequest.DeviceOrderId is the till's own id, unique per tenant, so a sync that
was cut off can be sent again and is answered with the order already posted. decimal SubmitOrderRequest.TotalDue is what the
receipt showed the customer: the server recomputes the totals and refuses the order when they differ, so a stale
catalogue is caught rather than booked.

SupplierAccountSummary.description: The account as saved plus the effective terms once the group's defaults are applied.

TableExportColumn.description: A column of a table export: its header and how its cells are typed (text, number or date).

TableExportRequest.description:
A table the web client already shows (a list's visible columns and rows, in its order), to be written as CSV or XLSX.
`documentType` names the kind of record listed, so a role that may not export that kind is refused.

TaxCodeReconciliation.description: A tax code's ledger movement on one account role against what the tax entries say it should be; a difference means a posting outside the tax module touched the account.

TaxDocumentLine.description:
A document line to tax: its amount on the document's basis, and either its item (whose tax group, the item's or its
category's, determines the code), an item tax group, or a code it names. Countries override the document's.

TaxDocumentRequest.description:
A whole document to tax. The partner's tax group is its customer (sales) or supplier (purchase) account's in the
company unless given; goods ship from the company's country on a sale and to it on a purchase unless given.

TaxedDocumentResult.description: A document taxed: its lines, per-code summary and totals, and why each line took its code. The rounding level is the regime's or the company's, whichever asks for document level (ADR-0005).

TaxedLine.description: A line's net, tax and gross; reverse charge lines carry the tax self-assessed on both sides but add nothing to the gross.

TaxReturnBox.description: One figure of a return: a box's taxable base and the tax on it, in the company's functional currency.

TaxReturnDrillDownLine.description: One tax entry behind a box figure, for the return's drill-down.

TaxReturnPreview.description:
A return computed from the tax ledger for a company, regime and period (ADR-0018): the boxes it reports, reconciled
to the tax accounts of the general ledger, and the net amount owed (positive) or due back (negative).

TaxSummary.description: A document's tax per code (for printing and posting) and its totals.

TenantSecurityPolicy.description: Security policy a tenant admin controls (stored in control.tenants.settings).

TenantSummary.description: The workspace as the client sees it; Edition picks the shell (full menus or the trader edition, ADR-0035).

TotpEnrolledResponse.description: TOTP enrolment confirmed during sign-in: the sign-in continues, and the recovery codes are shown once.

TraderApplyPricesRequest.description: Writes prices into the sales price list (the board's list, or the one named) from today.

TraderCashAccount.description: A bank account or cash box with its balance today, in its currency and the company's.

TraderCashMovement.description: One movement of a cash box or bank account in the trader's words: what came in or went out, and the balance after it.

TraderCashReport.description: The cash and bank screen (ADR-0035 §18): every box and account of the company over the period asked for (to today when no end is given).

TraderCashReportAccount.description: A cash box or bank account over the period: its balance now, what it held when the period began, what came in and went out, what it held at the period's end, and its movements newest first.

TraderDailyRate.description: One currency the trader buys in: the spot rate to the company's currency in force today, the date it was entered from, and whether it was entered for today.

TraderDailyRates.description: The day's rates (ADR-0035 §14): whether the prompt is due now (the hour reached and a currency without today's rate), the hour it is asked from (negative: never), and each currency's rate.

TraderDailyRatesRequest.description: Today's spot rates entered in one go, 1 unit of each currency = the rate in the company's currency; a reason when a rate of today is corrected.

TraderHealth.description: The health of the project (ADR-0035 §8): one read over the modules' contracts, nothing kept.

TraderIncome.description:
The income statement of a period in a trader's words, tied to the ledger like the shipped profit and loss: what was
sold, what came back or was discounted, what the goods sold had cost, the profit on them, the other income, the
expenses by name, the bank and exchange costs, the income tax, and what is left. Costs and expenses are positive;
a profit is positive and a loss negative.

TraderIncomeLine.description: One named expense of the period (rent, salaries, utilities): the account's name is the trader's word for it.

TraderMarketRate.description: Today's spot rate from a purchase currency to the company's, or null when none is entered under Rates.

TraderMonthResult.description: One month of results for the trend.

TraderOwnerMoney.description: The owner's money in the business (ADR-0035 §12): what was put in and taken out in all, the equity accounts each goes to, and the movements newest first.

TraderOwnerMovement.description: One movement as the trader reads it back: the journal that holds it, its kind, the box, the amount, the note, and whether it still stands.

TraderOwnerMovementRequest.description: Money the owner puts in or takes out: which, from or into which bank account or cash box, how much in the company's currency, on which day, and a note.

TraderPricingBoard.description: The board: the list priced, the settings in force, today's market rates and every item with a cost or a price. Hints: no_price_list.

TraderPricingRow.description:
One item on the pricing board: what it cost landed (from its latest shipment), what it would cost to buy again at
today's rate, the cost the trader entered on the item when the program knows no other, the price it sells at now
and the margin that leaves, the suggested price at the target margin, the floor below which a unit sells at a loss
(the cost basis rounded up to the increment), and the alerts (no_price, no_cost, no_market_rate, loss_at_cost,
loss_at_replacement, margin_below_target, rate_up, rate_down).

TraderReorderRow.description: An item the stock and the shipments on the way will not carry through the cover days at the pace of the last cover days' sales, and how many to order.

TraderSalesByCustomer.description: What one customer bought in the period, net, and the share of the period's sales.

TraderSalesByItem.description: What one item brought in the period: the quantity sold, the net sales in the company's currency and their share of the period's sales.

TraderShipmentUnderway.description: A shipment on the way: its stage, dates, the goods in the order's currency and the company's, what was paid for them, the journey's costs so far and the hints of the shipment screen.

TraderViability.description:
Whether the project carries itself: the fixed costs of a month (the trader's setting, else the average of the last
three months' expenses, else unknown), the margin that pays them (this period's gross margin, else the pricing
target), the sales a month needs to break even, this month's sales so far and where they lead at this pace, the
money in the banks and boxes, what is owed to and by the trader, and how many months the cash covers the fixed costs.

TraderWarning.description: Something to act on, as a code the client words with the value where one helps: loss, fixed_costs_unknown, cash_negative (amount), cash_runway_short (months), break_even_not_covered (percent), margin_below_target (percent), overdue_receivables (amount), overdue_payables (amount), shipments_attention (count), no_recent_sales (days), reorder_needed (count).

TransferQuantityRequest.description:
A quantity for one line of a ship or receive, in the line's unit; lines left out take everything outstanding. On a
receipt, Shortage is what shipped but never arrived: it is written off from transit with the reason code.

UnreconciledAgingRow.description: Book movements the bank has not confirmed yet, by how long they have waited.

ValidateExpressionRequest.description: For the on_block trigger the fields come from the block's values, so unknown names are allowed.

WebhookCreated.description: Returned once, at creation and rotation: the secret is stored encrypted and never shown again.

WidgetDefinition.description: A widget as saved: its source (a saved report by id, or a statement layout by id or shipped code), how it is drawn, its period and width (of four columns).

WidgetKpi.description: A KPI: one figure, the comparable figure of the prior window when the source carries one, and how to format it.

WidgetOptions.description: How a widget reads its source: the chart options of a chart widget, the measure of a KPI over a report, the row and column of a KPI over a statement, the closing-entry choice of a statement.

WriteOffRequest.description: Writes off what is still open on an item, or part of it: as bad debt, or as a small balance not worth chasing.
